root: generative pipeline for discovery of single phase immersion coolants
gaps: No published work runs Green-Kubo viscosity and thermal conductivity over a 100–1000 candidate ester shortlist; the closest prior (Imperial/Dini-Ewen) covers only eight molecules, two of which are esters.
Nobody has MD-verified the Org-Mol 461-monoester ranking, so the card's check-first (OPLS-AA reproducing Ester 1's 6.41 cSt within ±25%) is untested.
LG AI Research validates immersion-coolant candidates by TGA/DSC and literature only, leaving viscosity/thermal conductivity of the ~92,861 shortlist physically unverified before selection.

LOPLS-AA's systematic under-prediction of viscosity for oxygen-containing (ester) molecules is documented at n=8 but unquantified at shortlist scale, so whether MD actually reorders a large ester ranking is genuinely open.

programmes.name: Org-Mol — SINOPEC Research Institute of Petroleum Processing / DP Technology / AI for Science Institute
programmes.step: The hand-off from the Org-Mol machine-learning shortlist to synthesis: after screening over 6 million esters and filtering 461 monoesters on predicted dielectric constant, viscosity and thermal conductivity, they pick candidates for synthesis manually. This is exactly the slot where the card inserts Green-Kubo MD verification of viscosity and thermal conductivity before synthesis.

activity.claim: The Org-Mol paper (the source of the 461-monoester shortlist) was published in npj Computational Materials on 11 July 2025; no later release from this collaboration was found.

claims.claim: The shortlist-to-synthesis step is handled today with machine-learning property models only — the kinetic viscosity model then the thermal conductivity model — with no molecular-dynamics verification in between.
The working shortlist is 461 monoesters, of which only two are actually synthesized and measured; the rest are never independently verified.
The team's stated reason for not running MD is cost at screening scale — a claim the card directly tests by parallelising Green-Kubo runs.

programmes.if_lever_changes: If MD reorders the shortlist, the team would stop selecting two candidates by manual synthetic feasibility from an unverified ML ranking: they would run Green-Kubo viscosity/thermal conductivity over the top 100–300 (or all 461) monoesters and synthesize MD-verified leaders, likely surfacing esters better than the two they measured, and the MD-verified points would become training data to correct the 22.5% MAPE viscosity model.
programmes.if_not_changes: If MD merely confirms the ML ranking unchanged from 100 through 1000 candidates, the published ML-only screening stays as-is and MD is demoted to an optional spot-check, so their practice changes nothing beyond a one-off validation of the pipeline.

already_done.claim: This team has not run the card's experiment: the 461 monoesters were ranked by ML models and only two were verified, experimentally by synthesis rather than by MD; no Green-Kubo viscosity/thermal conductivity verification of the shortlist was performed.

programmes.name: LG AI Research — GATE (Geometrically Aligned Transfer Encoder)
programmes.step: The final validation stage (Fig. 2f) of their five-stage AI-enabled high-throughput screening workflow for single-phase immersion cooling fluids: after GATE screens billions of candidates down to a shortlist, the chosen few are validated before deployment. The card's MD verification of viscosity and thermal conductivity targets this validation step.

activity.claim: LG AI Research's GATE immersion-coolant paper was posted to arXiv on 27 October 2025 and last revised 31 October 2025 (v2), the most recent release found.

claims.claim: Validation today is experimental (TGA, DSC) plus literature values; transport properties like viscosity and thermal conductivity that their instruments cannot measure are taken from the literature rather than computed by MD.

The screening operates at billion-molecule scale but narrows to only four experimentally verified candidates, so most shortlisted molecules never get a physics-based check of their viscosity/thermal conductivity.
Four finalists are the extent of their verification stage; the pipeline is run by LG AI Research with Kyonggi University.

programmes.if_lever_changes: If MD reorders a 100–1000 candidate shortlist, LG AI Research would gain a physics-based verification stage to insert between GATE's 92,861-molecule shortlist and its 4-candidate experimental validation — re-ranking viscosity/thermal conductivity by Green-Kubo before purchase/synthesis and catching candidates GATE mis-orders, rather than relying on literature values.
programmes.if_not_changes: If MD only confirms GATE's ranking, the existing literature-plus-TGA/DSC validation remains sufficient and MD verification would not earn a permanent place in their pipeline, so their practice would be unchanged.

already_done.claim: LG AI Research has not run MD verification of viscosity/thermal conductivity on their shortlist; their validation stage is experimental measurement and literature survey only.

programmes.name: Imperial College London Tribology Group (Dini) / Ewen (Bath) — MD-vs-ML thermophysical benchmarking
programmes.step: Their head-to-head benchmark of machine-learning models against equilibrium molecular-dynamics (Green-Kubo) simulations for density, viscosity and thermal conductivity of organic liquids (lubricant- and cooling-fluid-sized molecules) — the exact property pair and force-field family the card deploys at shortlist scale.

activity.claim: The paper was published in Digital Discovery (RSC) with version of record dated 29 September 2026, a few weeks before this search.

claims.claim: Their MD practice today is Green-Kubo equilibrium MD on only eight molecules — two each from four chemical families including esters — at 40 and 100 °C, i.e. n=8 rather than the card's 100–1000.
They use the same OPLS-family force field the card specifies, run in LAMMPS.

They already found chemistry-dependent force-field error for the property pair the card targets: viscosity is under-predicted for oxygen-containing (ester/ether) molecules, though the reference ranking is largely preserved.

programmes.if_lever_changes: If MD measurably reorders a 100–1000 candidate shortlist, their current conclusion that ML alone is 'well suited to high-throughput screening' would need revision: they would have to recommend MD as a verification stage before synthesis for immersion coolants, contradicting their n=8 finding that MD adds little over ML for ranking.
programmes.if_not_changes: If MD merely confirms the ML ranking, it corroborates their existing result that 'the reference ranking of the fluids is nonetheless largely preserved' by MD — so their practice stays as published: ML for screening, MD only as an extrapolation/force-field sanity check.

already_done.claim: This group has already run a smaller version of the card's experiment — Green-Kubo EMD viscosity and thermal conductivity of organic liquids (including esters) benchmarked against ML — but on eight molecules, not a 100–1000 candidate shortlist and not the Org-Mol 461 esters; their finding that LOPLS-AA under-predicts ester viscosity bears directly on the card's OPLS-AA check-first tolerance.
